tools.name: device_fpga_de10lite_program
tools.description: Burn a Quartus .sof bitstream to a DE10-Lite (or any USB-Blaster-attached MAX10/Cyclone board) via quartus_pgm. v0.66 adds a mandatory pre-burn RTL static-auditor gate: when rtl_dir is provided, every v0.63/v0.64 auditor (tristate self-rx mask, pulse decoder edge, packet length check, OTP write lock, L12 sequence impl, timer freeze after state) runs on that source tree and any FAIL refuses the burn (unless allow_known_bugs=true). v0.119.52 (Wave 20) adds a second pre-burn RTL repair guard: the SOF's resolved project root is audited via `flow_compliance_check.py --phase 2 --strict-structural`; any structural-gate FAIL blocks the burn (BURN_BLOCKED_STRUCTURAL_GATES_FAIL) until the RTL repair/retry loop converges, unless the caller explicitly passes `bypass_pre_burn_check=true` for emergency override. Returns success status, programmer output tail, resolved cable / device index, the precheck report, and the flow_compliance verdict for provenance.

sof_path.description: Absolute path to the .sof bitstream to program (host-side).

cable_name.description: Quartus programmer cable name. 'USB-Blaster' picks the first one found.

device_index.description: Index of the device in the JTAG chain (1-based; DE10-Lite has only one device).

rtl_dir.description: v0.66: directory of .v/.sv files that were synthesized into sof_path. When provided, rtl_precheck_gate runs here before burn and any auditor FAIL blocks the burn. Strongly recommended — skipping means you are asserting the SOF is trusted without source review.

l12_json.description: Path to L12_BEHAVIORAL_SEQUENCES.json for the l12_sequence_implementation_check auditor (forwarded to rtl_precheck_gate).

allow_known_bugs.description: If true, a precheck FAIL is surfaced in the response but does NOT block the burn. Intended only for intentional debug flows ('I know it has bug X, I want to measure it anyway'). Audit trail still records which auditor failed.

skip_rtl_precheck.description: If true, do not invoke rtl_precheck_gate at all. Use for pre-built 3rd-party SOFs whose matching RTL source is not on this host. Asserts the SOF is trusted by the caller.

waive_auditors.description: v0.99.3: per-auditor waiver. List of auditor names (e.g. ["pulse_decoder_edge_check", "fsm_error_invariant"]) to selectively waive. If EVERY failing auditor is in this list, the burn proceeds with status=PASS_WITH_WAIVER. Any unwaived failure still blocks. Replaces all-or-nothing allow_known_bugs for projects where one auditor is known to false-flag.

bypass_pre_burn_check.description: v0.119.52 (Wave 20): emergency override. Set true to skip the pre-burn flow_compliance --phase 2 --strict-structural audit. Use ONLY for burning known-PASS oracle SOFs whose project tree is not on this host, or for explicit manual debug flows. Setting this false (default) hard-blocks the burn whenever any structural-RTL gate FAILs — closes the silent process violation observed in the 25th fresh-agent benchmark.

post_burn_scope_checks.description: v0.66: JSON-encoded list of scope-check dicts forwarded to scope_periodic_pulse_check.py after a successful burn. Each entry: {name, channel, span_ms, period_ms, pulse_min_us, pulse_max_us, expect (present/absent), min_periodic, trigger_timeout_s, save_csv}. Any FAIL flips overall success to False so the caller discovers silicon-vs-spec drift within seconds of the burn rather than two days later via manual probe. Example: [{"name":"post_por_wake_active","channel":4,"span_ms":100,"period_ms":5,"expect":"present","min_periodic":5}]

tools.name: device_fpga_de10lite_detect
tools.description: List USB-Blaster JTAG cables visible to Quartus and the chained devices on each. Returns { cables: [{ name, devices: [{idx, id_hex, name}] }] }. Useful for sanity-checking hardware before invoking program.

tools.name: device_fpga_de10lite_adc_read
tools.description: Read analog voltage from DE10-Lite MAX10 internal 12-bit ADC via JTAG system-console. v0.108: hardware-in-the-loop analog verification. Requires an FPGA design with the ADC Controller Intel FPGA IP instantiated and the JTAG-to-Avalon bridge connected. Returns averaged raw ADC code and computed voltage in mV.

channel.description: ADC channel (0-7, mapped to MAX10 analog input pins ADC_INn).

samples.description: Number of ADC samples to average for noise reduction.

reference_mv.description: ADC reference voltage in mV. MAX10 internal reference is 2.5V.

adc_base_addr.description: Avalon-MM base address of the ADC Controller IP (from Platform Designer).

resources.name: programmer_status
resources.description: Live read of USB-Blaster JTAG cables visible to Quartus and the devices on each chain. No programming, no side effects — just runs `quartus_pgm --list` then `--auto` per cable. Lets MCP clients introspect 'is the FPGA plugged in and what's on the JTAG chain?' before invoking the program tool.
